what: Comparing expected-rank cuts and single-outcome gradings
title: Grading Alabama counties on income and incarceration
text: alabama$reference$actions stores single-criterion gradings optimized income alone (D1) incarceration alone (D2), -unordered vector (B0), expected-rank contiguous-cut rule (B3, sorts counties weighted expected rank chooses optimal contiguous cutpoints along fixed order). evaluate four fixed vectors two-criterion loss using postrank_compare(): Two-criterion loss (weights 0.5/0.5, tau = 0.20, G_max = 5) pool common grading four fixed reference gradings. dataset, unrestricted common grading (joint) expected-rank cut rule (B3) produce identical grades pair relations (loss 0.150394, 1,249 ordered pairs), joint mixed-integer programming (MIP) search offers zero loss reduction beyond B3 (additionally supplying unrestricted lower bound across 5-grade groupings). Evaluating D1 (Income alone) D2 (Incarceration alone) two-criterion loss gives 0.190573 0.199764. Conversely, can evaluate much extra single-criterion loss shared common grading incurs outcome relative D1 D2 objectives: Requiring one shared grading across outcomes adds 0.054824 expected loss income (0.116403 versus 0.061578) 0.064528 incarceration (0.184385 versus 0.119857), equal-weight average extra loss 0.059676 (measured expected-loss units rather dollars posterior score intervals).
code: comparison <- postrank_compare(common,   `Expected-rank cuts` = alabama$reference$actions$B3,   `Income alone` = alabama$reference$actions$D1,   `Incarceration alone` = alabama$reference$actions$D2,   `Withhold all` = alabama$reference$actions$B0,   baselines = character() ) knitr::kable(comparison$table[, c("method", "risk", "N", "G")],   digits = 6, row.names = FALSE,   col.names = c("Report", "Two-criterion loss", "Ordered pairs", "Grades")) postrank_plot_compare(comparison) single <- alabama$reference$single_criterion single_loss <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(single)), function(i) {   crit <- single$criterion[i]   postrank_evaluate(alabama$reference$actions[[single$method[i]]],     alabama$alternatives[[crit]], weights = setNames(1, crit),     tau = 0.20)$primary_risk }, numeric(1)) common_loss <- profile$risk[match(single$criterion, profile$criterion)] cost <- data.frame(   Criterion = single$criterion,   Common = common_loss,   Separate = single_loss,   Difference = common_loss - single_loss,   Archived_gap = single$gap ) knitr::kable(cost, digits = 6, row.names = FALSE,   col.names = c("Criterion", "Common loss", "Separate loss",     "Extra loss for common grades", "Separate solver gap"))

JSON file stores schema_version = "applied-0.1". object R keeps value input_schema_version uses schema_version = "0.1.0" -memory layout. package ships complete example file, examples/synthetic-iid.json, holding 32-draw, three-entity ("001", "site-B", "site C"), two-criterion synthetic normal sample postrank_toy: companion script examples/make-synthetic-input.R defines make_postrank_synthetic_input() without running source() restores caller’s random-number state; regenerating list converting as_postrank_draws() matches stored sample within 1e-12 across platforms: write_postrank_draws() formats numbers 17-digit precision reading file back reproduces floating-point draw array identically, read_postrank_draws() rejects duplicate JSON keys, malformed numbers, --range integers, invalid Unicode surrogates:
code: path <- system.file("examples", "synthetic-iid.json",   package = "postrank", mustWork = TRUE) toy_draws <- read_postrank_draws(path) toy_draws[c("input_schema_version", "schema_version")] #> $input_schema_version #> [1] "applied-0.1" #>  #> $schema_version #> [1] "0.1.0" toy_draws[["entity_ids"]] #> [1] "001"    "site-B" "site C" toy_draws[["criterion_ids"]] #> [1] "need_A" "need_B" dim(toy_draws[["joint_draws"]][["tensor"]][["values"]]) #> [1] 32  3  2 generator <- system.file("examples", "make-synthetic-input.R",   package = "postrank", mustWork = TRUE) source(generator) toy_spec <- make_postrank_synthetic_input() rebuilt <- as_postrank_draws(toy_spec) rebuilt_values <- rebuilt[["joint_draws"]][["tensor"]][["values"]] stored_values <- toy_draws[["joint_draws"]][["tensor"]][["values"]] max(abs(rebuilt_values - stored_values)) <= 1e-12 #> [1] TRUE toy_spec[["targets"]][[1]][c("criterion_id", "estimand", "units")] #> $criterion_id #> [1] "need_A" #>  #> $estimand #> [1] "Toy latent site need under the explicitly specified independent Normal target law" #>  #> $units #> [1] "toy real-valued need units" copy_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".json") write_postrank_draws(toy_draws, copy_path) roundtrip <- read_postrank_draws(copy_path) identical(roundtrip[["joint_draws"]][["tensor"]][["values"]], stored_values) #> [1] TRUE unlink(copy_path)

what: Input validation versus statistical model checking
title: Preparing your posterior draws and comparison probabilities
text: Input validation checks object structure required descriptions present; check whether statistical model appropriate, whether targets identified, whether MCMC chains converged. Omitting eight required blocks postrank_declarations() stops error, can inspect validation flags returned validate_postrank_draws() directly: valid TRUE array dimensions, axis names, finite values, ties, eight required descriptions passed package’s R checks. schema_checked FALSE route uses external JSON Schema validator. source_values_checked FALSE example supplied array directly. import posterior object, as_postrank_posterior() compares mapped values source records result. jointness_verified convergence_verified remain FALSE routes. Assessing dependence convergence requires evidence fitted model sampling run. input (draws, mcmc_draws, analytic, probability_input) ready, pass postrank() chosen policy settings solver. Gurobi default solver requires license; call (eval = FALSE) selects open-source HiGHS solver (install.packages("highs")):
code: tryCatch(   postrank_declarations(targets = declarations[["targets"]],     context = declarations[["context"]]),   error = conditionMessage ) #> [1] "$.declarations: missing required scientific declarations: provenance, origin, identification_note, tie_justification, joint_generation, sampling_provenance (they are not inferred or filled with placeholders)" validation <- validate_postrank_draws(draws) validation[c("valid", "schema_checked", "source_values_checked",              "jointness_verified", "convergence_verified")] #> $valid #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $schema_checked #> [1] FALSE #>  #> $source_values_checked #> [1] FALSE #>  #> $jointness_verified #> [1] FALSE #>  #> $convergence_verified #> [1] FALSE result <- postrank(draws, weights = c(score_A = 1), tau = 0.25,   G_max = 3L, backend = "highs", level = 0.90,   control = postrank_control(time_limit = 30), fragility = FALSE)

title: Reading and exporting grading results
text: Printing one shows entity grade counts (6 entities 3 grades), posterior loss (0.0417), ordered (“disclosed”, 12) unordered (“withheld”, 3) pair counts, solver status gap, warnings. Grade 1 highest priority, sharing grade leaves pair unordered without claiming two sites equal scores; see Getting started: grading one two criteria. summary(one) adds policy settings (weights, G_max, tau), per-criterion table, availability optional summaries, full text recorded warnings. Optional results:, "unsupported input" (Monte Carlo fragility, requested default yet requires posterior draws rather analytic normal distribution) distinct "requested" (meaning FALSE passed checking input support: crossfit = TRUE also requires joint draws, whereas diagnostics = TRUE normal input evaluates conditional-normal summaries "Monte Carlo diagnostics" label). Neither label means value zero, summary() never runs new calculations. joint IID MCMC draw inputs, postrank() computes pairwise Monte Carlo fragility default leaving cross-fitting full trace diagnostics unless requested. can inspect extras fragility$summary stored 30-site, three-criterion draw analysis (analysis_30x3_tau35): pair flagged fragile estimated weighted error likelier direction within z = 2 Monte Carlo standard errors tau; pairwise flags descriptive summaries simulation noise need change jointly chosen grades (diagnostics = TRUE crossfit = TRUE, inspect x$diagnostics x$crossfit; see Monte Carlo diagnostics, cross-fitting, IID bounds). add input problem identity hashes, package solver versions, source descriptions console summary, set details = TRUE. capture formatted console lines character vector (matching exported format_postrank_*_cli() wrappers), call format(): Printing detailed displays extra provenance lines (including note "Bounds solver values; gap regret", regret means excess loss relative best grading true posterior), cat(..., sep = "\n") writes captured format() lines log file. scripts, extract numbers accessors rather parsing printed console text.
code: print(one) #> <postrank_analysis>  6 entities in 3 grades (sizes 2 / 2 / 2) #>   One criterion: score_A. #>   Posterior loss: 0.0417. #>   Disclosed 12 of 15 pairs (80.0%); withheld 3. #>   Expected error among disclosed pairs: score_A 0.002. #>   Solver: Optimal within solver tolerances. #>   Optimization gap: 0; requested absolute gap 1e-08. #>   Prepared: report card. #>   Grade 1 has highest priority; a shared grade withholds the comparison. #>   grade 1 (2): A, B #>   grade 2 (2): C, D #>   grade 3 (2): E, F #>   !  1 warning recorded: Reported lower bound exceeded the validated action ris... #>   i summary(x) explains the loss, settings and bounds; get_grades(x) returns #>     all grades. summary(one) #> <postrank_analysis_summary> #> Result: #>   6 entities in 3 grades (sizes 2 / 2 / 2). #>   One criterion: score_A. #>   Posterior loss: 0.0417. #>   Disclosed 12 of 15 pairs (80.0%); withheld 3. #>   Expected error among disclosed pairs: score_A 0.002. #> Settings: #>   Loss: the weighted average of criterion losses. #>   At most 3 grades; fewer may be used. #>   Withholding cost (tau): 0.2 per withheld pair. #> Criterion results: #>    Criterion Weight Loss   Error / disclosed #>    score_A   1      0.0417 0.002 #> Reading the loss: #>   Grade 1 has highest priority. A shared grade withholds that pair's comparison. #>   Each criterion loss averages expected errors on disclosed pairs and the #>     withholding cost over all unordered pairs. #>   Error / disclosed uses only the disclosed pairs; it is NA when their count is #>     zero. Tau is a loss cost, not an error-rate limit. #> Computation: #>   Solver: Optimal within solver tolerances. #>   Optimization gap: 0; requested absolute gap 1e-08. #>   Loss upper bound: 0.0417; lower bound: 0.0417. #>   Solver: highs; elapsed time 0.339 seconds. #>   The gap concerns optimization of the supplied probabilities. It does not #>     measure posterior uncertainty or Monte Carlo error. #> Optional results: #>   Report card: available. #>   Monte Carlo fragility: unsupported for this input. #>   Cross-fit check: not requested. #>   Monte Carlo diagnostics: not requested. #> Input assumptions: #>   Losses describe the supplied posterior and target definitions; source #>     declarations are not independently verified. #>   A low posterior loss does not verify the statistical model. #> Recorded warnings: #>   Reported lower bound exceeded the validated action risk by at most the #>     objective tolerance; it was clamped to the action risk (absolute gap 0). This #>     reflects floating-point rounding or solver tolerances, not a numerical #>     certificate. #>   i summary(x, details = TRUE) adds source records and identities; structured #>     fields remain available. a35 <- postrank_example("analysis_30x3_tau35") do.call(rbind, lapply(a35[["extras"]], function(e) {   data.frame(requested = e[["requested"]], available = e[["available"]],     reason = if (is.null(e[["reason"]])) "" else e[["reason"]]) })) #>             requested available        reason #> report_card      TRUE      TRUE               #> fragility        TRUE      TRUE               #> crossfit        FALSE     FALSE not_requested #> diagnostics     FALSE     FALSE not_requested a35[["fragility"]][["summary"]][c("pairs", "traced", "fragile",   "fragile_disclosed", "fragile_tied")] #> $pairs #> [1] 435 #>  #> $traced #> [1] 43 #>  #> $fragile #> [1] 20 #>  #> $fragile_disclosed #> [1] 14 #>  #> $fragile_tied #> [1] 6 detailed <- summary(one, details = TRUE) head(format(one, width = 72, tier = 2), 4) #> [1] "<postrank_analysis>  6 entities in 3 grades (sizes 2 / 2 / 2)" #> [2] "  One criterion: score_A."                                     #> [3] "  Posterior loss: 0.0417."                                     #> [4] "  Disclosed 12 of 15 pairs (80.0%); withheld 3."

title: Reading and exporting grading results
text: default, .data.frame() returns two-column data frame character entity_id integer grade original input entity order. Calling .data.frame() postrank_analysis, postrank_fit, postrank_baseline always returns two columns, whether report card prepared: Join results back entity metadata entity_id rather row position formatted display labels. extract marginal posterior summaries alongside grades, request = "report_card": Along entity_id grade, card includes sort_rank, pair counts entity (n_above, n_below, n_withheld), per-criterion columns mean_<criterion>, lower_<criterion>, upper_<criterion>, expected_rank_<criterion> (90% equal-tail marginal score intervals). criterion negated input construction (orientation = "lower"), columns remain negated scale, negating back raw units swaps lower_<criterion> upper_<criterion>. Select columns name rather column index. marginal posterior skewed, posterior mean can sit outside equal-tail interval, report-card tables plots show stored values unchanged; likewise, inputs carry precomputed intervals one level (90% pr_case_cde pr_case_krw, 95% pr_case_alabama) recompute interval levels. Rows .data.frame(x, = "report_card") ordered grade report card’s secondary sort rule (sort_rank), can differ original input order: report card built (example, input supplies pairwise comparison probabilities without marginal intervals), calling .data.frame(x, = "report_card") stops error explaining unavailable, .data.frame(x) still returns two-column grade table.
code: grade_table <- as.data.frame(one) grade_table #>   entity_id grade #> 1         A     1 #> 2         B     1 #> 3         C     2 #> 4         D     2 #> 5         E     3 #> 6         F     3 identical(grade_table$entity_id, sites$one$entity_ids) #> [1] TRUE identical(grade_table, as.data.frame(one$fit)) #> [1] TRUE card <- as.data.frame(one, what = "report_card") names(card) #>  [1] "entity_id"             "grade"                 "sort_rank"             #>  [4] "n_above"               "n_below"               "n_withheld"            #>  [7] "mean_score_A"          "lower_score_A"         "upper_score_A"         #> [10] "expected_rank_score_A" knitr::kable(card[, c("entity_id", "grade", "mean_score_A",   "lower_score_A", "upper_score_A")], digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,   col.names = c("Entity", "Grade", "Mean", "Interval lower", "Interval upper")) list(   input_order = as.data.frame(two)$entity_id,   report_card_order = as.data.frame(two, what = "report_card")$entity_id ) #> $input_order #> [1] "A" "B" "C" "D" "E" "F" #>  #> $report_card_order #> [1] "A" "C" "B" "D" "E" "F"

what: Extracting grades, pair relations, profiles, and loss
title: Reading and exporting grading results
text: get_grades() returns integer vector named entity_id. get_relations() returns n x n integer matrix entry [, j] 1 row entity placed higher-priority grade column entity j, -1 opposite order, 0 pair shares grade (diagonal). Thus [ "", "B" ] 0 (left unordered) [ "", "C" ] 1 (ordered C). get_profile(), E posterior expected number wrong-direction ordered pairs criterion, E_over_N divides E number ordered pairs N, E_over_M divides E M pairs, risk adds unordered-pair cost tau * (M - N) / M: multiple criteria, get_profile(two) one row per criterion, get_risk(two) returns named list (risk, lower_bound, gap, status) overall objective (weighted average criterion losses default, worst-criterion loss objective = "minimax"). can also evaluate fixed integer grade vector input without running solver via postrank_evaluate(). Placing every site grade 1 leaves pairs unordered: N 0, E_over_N NA (0) primary_risk equals tau (0.2). -unordered report valid one-grade action, distinct failed timed-solver run returned checked grading.
code: grades <- get_grades(one) grades #> A B C D E F  #> 1 1 2 2 3 3 relations <- get_relations(one) relations[c("A", "B", "C"), c("A", "B", "C")] #>         entity_j #> entity_i  A  B C #>        A  0  0 1 #>        B  0  0 1 #>        C -1 -1 0 profile <- get_profile(one) knitr::kable(profile[, c("criterion", "weight", "E", "E_over_M",   "E_over_N", "risk")], digits = 5, row.names = FALSE) risk <- get_risk(one) risk #> $risk #> [1] 0.04165164 #>  #> $lower_bound #> [1] 0.04165164 #>  #> $gap #> [1] 0 #>  #> $status #> [1] "optimal" N <- sum(relations[upper.tri(relations)] != 0L) M <- choose(length(grades), 2) tau <- 0.2 c(from_parts = (profile$E + tau * (M - N)) / M, stored = risk$risk) #> from_parts     stored  #> 0.04165164 0.04165164 withheld <- postrank_evaluate(   setNames(rep(1L, length(grades)), names(grades)), sites$one,   weights = c(score_A = 1), tau = 0.2 ) withheld[c("N", "E_over_N", "primary_risk")] #> $N #> [1] 0 #>  #> $E_over_N #> score_A  #>      NA  #>  #> $primary_risk #> [1] 0.2

what: Saving CSV tables and RDS objects
title: Reading and exporting grading results
text: Use CSV exporting flat tables software, RDS saving complete postrank_analysis object R settings, report card, solver bounds, warnings intact. write fresh temporary folder: Specify colClasses = c(entity_id = "character", grade = "integer") reading CSV files back R leading zeros IDs "01001" preserved, row.names = FALSE writing extra row-number column added. Keep postrank version source input alongside archived .rds files long-term reproducibility.
code: export_dir <- tempfile("postrank-exports-") dir.create(export_dir) csv_file <- file.path(export_dir, "grades.csv") rds_file <- file.path(export_dir, "analysis.rds") write.csv(grade_table, csv_file, row.names = FALSE) csv_again <- read.csv(csv_file,   colClasses = c(entity_id = "character", grade = "integer")) identical(csv_again, grade_table) #> [1] TRUE saveRDS(one, rds_file) restored <- readRDS(rds_file) identical(get_grades(restored), grades) #> [1] TRUE identical(get_risk(restored), risk) #> [1] TRUE identical(as.data.frame(restored, what = "report_card"), card) #> [1] TRUE

title: Figures and sensitivity to reporting settings
text: reference two-criterion grading orders N = 9 M = 15 site pairs leaves 6 pairs unordered. default (show = "E_over_N"), postrank_plot_profile() divides criterion’s expected wrong-direction count E shared count 9 ordered pairs: Posterior expected wrong-direction errors per ordered pair (E/N) Score Score B reference two-criterion grading, point size proportional criterion weight. Expected wrong-direction errors per ordered pair 1.77% (0.0177) score_A 2.67% (0.0267) score_B. Setting show = "E_over_M" divides E M = 15 pairs instead (1.06% 1.60%), show = "risk" adds unordered-pair cost tau * (M - N) / M (0.0906 0.0960). three quantities posterior expectations rather counts observed mistakes. grading leaves pairs unordered (N = 0), E_over_N NA postrank_plot_profile() omits point note; similarly, missing unvalidated grid points leave gaps along postrank_plot_frontier() lines. Read omitted point object’s status N rather treating empty panel zero error.
code: library(postrank) sites <- pr_tutorial one <- postrank_example("tutorial_one") two <- postrank_example("tutorial_two") entity_labels <- setNames(sites$units$label, sites$units$entity_id) criterion_labels <- c(score_A = "Score A", score_B = "Score B") profile_plot <- postrank_plot_profile(two, show = "E_over_N",   criterion_labels = criterion_labels) profile_plot profile_data <- postrank_plot_data(two, "profile") profile_data[, c("criterion", "weight", "E", "E_over_N", "E_over_M", "risk")] #>   criterion weight         E   E_over_N   E_over_M       risk #> 1   score_A    0.5 0.1596996 0.01774440 0.01064664 0.09064664 #> 2   score_B    0.5 0.2405960 0.02673289 0.01603973 0.09603973

title: Figures and sensitivity to reporting settings
text: postrank_settings_grid() builds grid policy settings around reference analysis keeping posterior fixed: changing tau alters cost leaving pairs unordered, changing weights alters criterion errors weighted loss, changing G_max alters many distinct grades allowed. default, postrank_settings_grid() varies one axis time around reference settings (7 settings rather full factorial cross-product): Recomputing sweep requires solver (Gurobi default needs license; backend = "highs" uses open-source highs package install.packages("highs")). solver call shown eval = FALSE, stored result loaded postrank_example(): Giving 0.8 weight score_A (A_heavy, row 6) lowers expected errors per ordered pair score_A 0.0021 (0.21%) raising score_B’s rate 0.2371 (23.71%) across 12 ordered pairs. Raising grade cap 3 4 (G_max=4, row 5) leaves grading unchanged (3 occupied grades, 9 ordered pairs, 0 changed pair relations), allowing extra grade force solver use . 7 rows finished status "optimal" maximum optimization gap 1.39e-17 (max(st$risk_absolute_gap)), two rows recording small floating-point lower-bound clamping within solver tolerance. gaps warnings describe optimization supplied probabilities; posterior intervals guarantees score model.
code: grid <- postrank_settings_grid(two$settings,   tau = c(0.1, 0.3), G_max = c(2L, 4L),   weights = list(     A_heavy = c(score_A = 0.8, score_B = 0.2),     B_heavy = c(score_A = 0.2, score_B = 0.8)   )) sensitivity <- postrank_sensitivity(two, grid, backend = "highs",   control = postrank_control(time_limit = 60, threads = 1, seed = 1304)) sensitivity <- postrank_example("tutorial_sensitivity") sg <- sensitivity$grid st <- sensitivity$table knitr::kable(data.frame(   Setting = sg$label, tau = sg$tau, Cap = sg$G_max,   `Weights A/B` = paste0(sg$w_score_A, "/", sg$w_score_B),   Grades = st$G, Ordered = st$N,   `A E/N` = round(st$E_over_N_score_A, 4),   `B E/N` = round(st$E_over_N_score_B, 4),   check.names = FALSE ), row.names = FALSE)

title: Figures and sensitivity to reporting settings
text: postrank_frontier() holds weights G_max fixed varying unordered-pair (“withholding”) cost tau across grid: Across five values tau, ordered-pair fraction (N/M) rises 0.533 0.800. panels show expected errors per ordered pair criterion overall loss. dashed vertical line marks reference setting 0.20. Along tau = 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40, report orders 8, 8, 9, 11, 12 15 pairs. first panel shows fraction N / M, rises 8/15 (0.533) 12/15 (0.800). Higher values tau penalize unordered pairs heavily never reduce exact optimal count ordered pairs posterior, weights, allowed grade family stay fixed. contrast, per-criterion error rates (E / N) need move monotonically: score_B, E / N rises 0.0267 tau = 0.20 0.1152 tau = 0.30 drops 0.0575 tau = 0.40 grade boundaries shift. point loss panel evaluates different value tau, connecting line segments aid visual reading rather defining intermediate gradings grid points. Even N grows tau, ordered pairs larger tau need contain every pair ordered smaller tau. Moving tau = 0.20 tau = 0.30 (tau=0.30, row 3) newly orders 3 pairs (n_new_disclosed) newly leaves 1 previously ordered pair unordered (n_new_withheld), net gain 2 ordered pairs: Pairwise ordering changes reference grading (tau = 0.20) higher-cost grading (tau = 0.30) across six sites.
code: frontier <- postrank_frontier(two, tau = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4),   backend = "highs",   control = postrank_control(time_limit = 60, threads = 1, seed = 1304)) frontier <- postrank_example("tutorial_frontier") frontier_plot <- postrank_plot_frontier(frontier, highlight = 0.2) frontier_plot hi_row <- which(sg$tau == 0.3) sensitivity$changes[hi_row, c("n_same", "n_new_disclosed", "n_new_withheld", "n_reversed")] #>   n_same n_new_disclosed n_new_withheld n_reversed #> 3     11               3              1          0 postrank_plot_relations(two, sensitivity$fits[[hi_row]],   entity_labels = entity_labels)

what: Comparing candidate gradings under one common loss
title: Figures and sensitivity to reporting settings
text: compare candidate gradings fairly, evaluate posterior input, weights, tau postrank_compare(). evaluate one-criterion score_A grading (get_grades(one)) -unordered one-grade vector alongside two-criterion common grading: two-criterion equal-weight loss tau = 0.20, score_A grading orders 12 pairs loss 0.1356, compared 0.0933 common grading (joint, 9 ordered pairs) 0.2000 leaving pairs unordered. postrank_compare() evaluates supplied grade vectors without re-optimizing (setting baselines = character() omits default expected_rank composite baseline cuts supplied gradings compared joint), postrank_plot_compare(comparison) plots either summary panels loss, disclosure, grade count (view = "summary") counts pairwise ordering differences joint (view = "relations"), marking candidate violates G_max, exact_G, q via family_feasible feasibility_reason (see Combining several criteria one common grading 30-site baseline comparison).
code: comparison <- postrank_compare(two,   `Score A grades` = get_grades(one),   `Withhold all` = setNames(rep(1L, nrow(sites$units)), sites$units$entity_id),   baselines = character()) knitr::kable(comparison$table[, c("method", "N", "G", "risk", "family_feasible")],   digits = 4, row.names = FALSE,   col.names = c("Grading", "Ordered pairs", "Grades", "Two-criterion loss", "Within G_max"))

what: Criterion-specific cost of sharing one common grading
title: Figures and sensitivity to reporting settings

what: Exact finite laws versus Monte Carlo draws
title: Posterior representations and pairwise comparison probabilities
text: postrank distinguishes two discrete state representations: Exact finite laws (exact_finite_posterior via as_postrank_draws()). discrete posterior defined completely integer-valued states θ(s)\theta^{(s)} positive integer probability numerators sharing common denominator (psp_s), eij=∑sps𝟏{θi(s)≤θj(s)} e_{ij} = \sum_s p_s \, \mathbf{1}\{\theta_i^{(s)} \le \theta_j^{(s)}\}  exact mathematical probability. Building aggregating exact_finite_posterior input requires suggested gmp package (install.packages("gmp")), checks exact integer masses retains exact rational probabilities postrank_pairwise() alongside double-precision array e (exact rational coefficients still make downstream floating-point sums MIP solves exact). Equal-weight posterior draws (postrank_draws(), postrank_draws_from_array(), as_postrank_posterior()). Retained simulation draws approximate underlying posterior sample average êij=1S∑s=1S𝟏{θi(s)≤θj(s)}. \widehat{e}_{ij} = \frac{1}{S} \sum_{s=1}^S \mathbf{1}\{\theta_i^{(s)} \le \theta_j^{(s)}\}.  Even êij\widehat{e}_{ij} equals 0 1 finite sample, true posterior probability need 0 1. Independent (regime = "iid") Markov chain Monte Carlo (regime = "mcmc") draws use sample average êij\widehat{e}_{ij} require different Monte Carlo uncertainty calculations, regime = "mcmc" records chain IDs, iteration numbers, warmup_per_chain, thin. Standard draw constructors require full numerical precision without observed within-criterion ties entities (round exported draws add random jitter, alters posterior) require equal weights 1 / S across retained draws (uneven importance weights accepted). postrank_toy (32 independent draws three entities two criteria), postrank_pairwise() aggregates e[, j, k] draw blocks without clipping empirical 0 1 entries, postrank_evaluate() evaluates fixed integer grading without running solver: Placing "001" Grade 1 leaving "site-B" "site C" together Grade 2 orders N = 2 M = 3 pairs. E_over_M divides expected errors M, E_over_N divides N. Supply positive integer grade labels, names(grade) matching entity_ids order. canonical_postrank_grade() renumbers occupied labels 1, ..., G preserving pair relations. criteria <- colnames(states[[1]])   decl <- tie_declarations(criteria, description)   as_postrank_tie_draws(c(list(     schema_version = "tie-aware-input-0.1", input_kind = "exact_finite_posterior",     dependence_mode = "joint_model", requested_functional = "expected_rank_loss",     entity_ids = ids, criterion_ids = criteria,     provenance = list(producer = "m4-ties-and-withholding", artifact_id = "law",       artifact_hash = digest::digest(list(states, masses), algo = "sha256"),       construction_note = "Exact finite distribution",       created_at = format(Sys.time(), tz = "UTC", format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")),     finite_law = list(denominator = sum(masses), value_representation = "safe_integer",       states = lapply(seq_along(states), function(s) list(         state_id = paste0("state-", s), mass_numerator = masses[s], theta = states[[s]])),       law_definition = description, not_empirical_posterior_relabeling = TRUE)   ), decl)) } input <- finite_input(states, masses,   "B equals 1; title: Monte Carlo diagnostics, cross-fitting, and IID bounds
text: Unlike pointwise MCSEs, postrank_iid_bounds() computes analytic simultaneous error radius across M=(n2)M = \binom{n}{2} unordered pairs criterion draws independent (regime = "iid") sample size fixed advance. standard postrank inputs tie-free (eji,k=1−eij,ke_{ji,k} = 1 - e_{ij,k}), bounding one direction per unordered pair bounds directions, giving 2M events per criterion (rather 4M tie-permitting formulation; tie-aware mode provide IID helpers). positive criterion error budgets αk\alpha_k summing α\alpha, radius criterion kk εk=min⁡{1,log⁡(2M/αk)2Sk}. \varepsilon_k = \min\!\left\{1,   \sqrt{\frac{\log(2M / \alpha_k)}{2 S_k}}\right\}. IID bounds protection envelopes hold stated conditions: Every criterion uses equal-weight independent (regime = "iid") entity-joint draws (pairs criteria need independent one another; MCMC draws rejected ESS IID sample size). Draw counts SkS_k allocations αk\alpha_k fixed sampling, adaptive_stopping = FALSE (design records declaration without verifying externally). 1−α1 - \alpha coverage statement refers repeated Monte Carlo sampling fixed posterior—posterior probability grading right check model specification. Formulas evaluated ordinary floating-point arithmetic without interval enclosures, guarantee_issued numerically_verified remain FALSE (guarantee_status = "conditional_bound"). postrank_toy, synthetic generator fixed S=32S = 32 α1=α2=0.025\alpha_1 = \alpha_2 = 0.025 (α=0.05\alpha = 0.05) sampling: Write δw=∑k=1Kwkεk\delta_w = \sum_{k=1}^K w_k \varepsilon_k. simultaneous 1−α1 - \alpha event every |êij,k−eij,k|≤εk|\widehat{e}_{ij,k} - e_{ij,k}| \le \varepsilon_k, empirical weighted loss fixed grading NN ordered pairs differs true posterior weighted loss (N/M)δw(N / M) \delta_w. Moreover, non-empty grading family fixed sampling (G_max exact_G, objective = "weighted" q = NULL), checked grading ĝ\widehat{g} verified whole-problem solver gap η=U−L\eta = U - L true posterior weighted-loss regret 2δw+η2 \delta_w + \eta. postrank_regret_bound() evaluates bound matching postrank_fit (bounding loss regret, equality grade vectors, rejecting raw, relative, candidate-gaps): weighted problem carries empirical error budgets q (Êk(g)≤qkN(g)\widehat{E}_k(g) \le q_k N(g)), Monte Carlo error also affects gradings appear feasible. postrank_protection_envelopes() constructs two shifted problems without running solver: inner_problem: tightened constraints Êk(g)≤(qk−εk)N(g)\widehat{E}_k(g) \le (q_k - \varepsilon_k) N(g); outer_problem: relaxed constraints Êk(g)≤(qk+εk)N(g)\widehat{E}_k(g) \le (q_k + \varepsilon_k) N(g). signed coefficients qk∓εkq_k \mp \varepsilon_k clipped (0, 1), zero-weight protected criteria still use εk\varepsilon_k. qk−εk<0q_k - \varepsilon_k < 0, grading N>0N > 0 can satisfy inner row, infeasible inner_problem prove true qq-constrained problem infeasible. Passing envelope postrank_protection_analysis() solves problems sequentially (requiring optimization solver highs licensed Gurobi) combines checked inner upper bound (inner_risk_upper) whole-problem outer lower bound (outer_whole_problem_risk_lower—never substituting inner lower bound) report computed_value equal inner_risk_upper - outer_whole_problem_risk_lower + 2 * delta_w (status = "diagnostic_only", guarantee_issued = FALSE). what: Two units, two domains, and identical marginal errors
title: Separate domain rules versus joint multidomain protection
text: Consider two units (B) across two domains (one two). normal state, B (2 > 1); reversed state, B (1 < 2). two discrete distributions identical marginal reversal probability 1/10 domain, differing whether reversals happen together separate states: set equal domain weights (1/2 default), unordered-pair cost tau = "1/4", strict error-proportion threshold t = "0", joint exceedance cap alpha = "3/20" using character strings exact rational values kept: two units, domain three possible grade columns: withhold (1, 1), A_above_B (1, 2), B_above_A (2, 1). Cartesian product contains nine two-domain cards (max_actions = 9L). Optimality postrank_mdomain_solve() holds within declared candidate set (exhausts two-unit profiles): nine candidates: coincident reversals nine candidates: disjoint reversals Reporting B domains additive loss 1/10 distributions, yet joint exceedance probability J 1/10 (<= 3/20, feasible) coincident 1/5 (> 3/20, infeasible) disjoint: dual card (B domains) joint laws disjoint, two cards tie minimum feasible loss (1/2)(1/10+1/4)=7/40(1/2)(1/10 + 1/4) = 7/40 joint exceedance probability 1/10—reporting B one domain leaving domain unordered: optimal feasible candidates declared sets Removing joint exceedance cap (t = NULL) restores separate domain optimization, making (B, B) optimal (risk = 1/10) laws—confirming union constraint coupled domains, pairing separate marginal simulations arbitrarily determine joint distribution applies:
code: units <- c("A", "B") domains <- c("one", "two") targets <- setNames(lapply(domains, function(d) list(   definition = paste("Fictional priority in domain", d),   units = "arbitrary priority units", orientation = "larger_is_higher",   equality_classes = units,   equality_provenance = "A and B are distinct modeled targets." )), domains)  make_states <- function(reverse, ids) {   x <- array(0, c(nrow(reverse), 2L, 2L), dimnames = list(ids, units, domains))   for (d in seq_along(domains)) {     x[, "A", d] <- ifelse(reverse[, d], 1, 2)     x[, "B", d] <- ifelse(reverse[, d], 2, 1)   }   x } make_law <- function(id, reverse, masses) {   postrank_mdomain_input(     make_states(reverse, paste0(id, "-", seq_len(nrow(reverse)))),     targets = targets,     provenance = list(       input_id = id, law_id = id, proper_law = TRUE,       joint_generation = "Complete finite support authored in this article.",       sampling_assumptions = list(         finite_support_origin = "All support states and exact masses listed here.")     ),     representation = "exact_finite_law", masses = masses) } laws <- list(   coincident = make_law("coincident",     rbind(c(FALSE, FALSE), c(TRUE, TRUE)), c("9/10", "1/10")),   disjoint = make_law("disjoint",     rbind(c(FALSE, FALSE), c(TRUE, FALSE), c(FALSE, TRUE)),     c("8/10", "1/10", "1/10")) ) policy <- postrank_mdomain_decision(tau = "1/4", t = "0", alpha = "3/20") columns <- list(withhold = c(A = 1L, B = 1L),   A_above_B = c(A = 1L, B = 2L), B_above_A = c(A = 2L, B = 1L)) families <- lapply(laws, postrank_mdomain_family,   columns = list(one = columns, two = columns), max_actions = 9L) fits <- setNames(lapply(names(laws), function(id) {   postrank_mdomain_solve(laws[[id]], families[[id]], policy, max_actions = 9L) }), names(laws)) column_label <- function(g) {   if (g[1L] == g[2L]) "withhold" else if (g[1L] < g[2L]) "A above B" else "B above A" } candidate_display <- function(fit) {   tab <- fit[["candidate_table"]]   actions <- fit[["solution"]][["actions"]][tab[["action_id"]]]   data.frame(     one = vapply(actions, function(g) column_label(g[, "one"]), ""),     two = vapply(actions, function(g) column_label(g[, "two"]), ""),     risk = tab[["risk_exact"]], joint_probability = tab[["J_exact"]],     feasible = tab[["feasible_for_represented_measure"]],     optimal = tab[["optimal"]], row.names = NULL   ) } knitr::kable(candidate_display(fits[["coincident"]]),   caption = "All nine candidates: coincident reversals") knitr::kable(candidate_display(fits[["disjoint"]]),   caption = "All nine candidates: disjoint reversals") dual <- matrix(c(1L, 2L, 1L, 2L), 2L, dimnames = list(units, domains)) dual_evaluations <- lapply(laws, postrank_mdomain_evaluate,   grades = dual, decision = policy) knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, lapply(names(laws), function(id) {   e <- dual_evaluations[[id]]   data.frame(law = id, error_one = e[["domain_table"]][["EF_exact"]][1L],     error_two = e[["domain_table"]][["EF_exact"]][2L], risk = e[["risk_exact"]],     joint_probability = e[["J_exact"]],     feasible = e[["feasible_for_represented_measure"]]) })), caption = "The same dual card (A above B in both domains) under both joint laws") optima <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(fits), function(id) {   tab <- candidate_display(fits[[id]])   data.frame(law = id, tab[tab[["optimal"]], ], row.names = NULL) })) knitr::kable(optima, caption = "All optimal feasible candidates in the declared sets") separable_policy <- postrank_mdomain_decision(tau = "1/4", t = NULL) separate_fits <- setNames(lapply(names(laws), function(id) {   postrank_mdomain_solve(laws[[id]], families[[id]], separable_policy, max_actions = 9L) }), names(laws)) knitr::kable(data.frame(   law = names(laws),   optimum_risk = vapply(separate_fits, function(f) f[["evaluation"]][["risk_exact"]], ""),   optimizer_count = vapply(separate_fits, `[[`, 1L, "optimizer_count") ))

what: Inspecting MCMC exceedance-event histories for a fixed multidomain card
title: Separate domain rules versus joint multidomain protection
text: inspect Markov chain explores exceedance event fixed report card, pass representation = "mcmc_equal_weight_draws" state_origin call postrank_mdomain_assess(..., method = "mcmc"). simulate two short unequal-length two-state Markov chains (24 31 iterations, transition probabilities 1/10 0 -> 1 2/5 1 -> 0, stationary reversal probability 1/5; illustrative lengths , independent 40-site file ): Next wrap two-chain history postrank_mdomain_input() evaluate postrank_mdomain_assess(..., method = "mcmc", batch_size = 10L) fixed dual card (B, B): Per-chain hit counts, max_zero_run, batch-level tables (assessment$native$batch_table, keeps trailing partial batches rather dropping ) summarize often chain visited exceedance event (combining chains unequal length, weight n_retained rather averaging unweighted chain rates). MCMC diagnostics descriptive summaries, guarantees: provide IID binomial certificate, prove convergence, turn split chains independent validation samples. See ?postrank_mdomain_assess fixed-sample method = "iid" design fields Grading entities across multiple domains step--step multidomain workflow.
code: simulate_chain <- function(n) {   z <- logical(n)   z[1L] <- stats::runif(1) < 1 / 5   for (i in 2:n) {     z[i] <- if (z[i - 1L]) stats::runif(1) >= 2 / 5 else stats::runif(1) < 1 / 10   }   z } set.seed(1202) chains <- list(chain_A = simulate_chain(24L), chain_B = simulate_chain(31L)) z <- unlist(chains, use.names = FALSE) history <- data.frame(   source_index = seq_along(z),   chain_id = rep(names(chains), lengths(chains)),   iteration_id = unlist(lapply(chains, seq_along), use.names = FALSE) ) history_input <- postrank_mdomain_input(   make_states(cbind(z, z), paste0("markov-", seq_along(z))), targets = targets,   provenance = list(     input_id = "tiny-markov-history", law_id = "tiny-markov-law", proper_law = TRUE,     joint_generation = "Both domains share the simulated binary chain state.",     retention = list(warmup_removed = 0L, thinning = 1L),     sampling_assumptions = list(       sampler = "Two-state Markov transition simulator.",       chain_details = "Lengths 24 and 31; stationary initial draws; seed 1202.",       target_assertion = "Stationary reversal probability 1/5.")   ),   representation = "mcmc_equal_weight_draws", state_origin = history) assessment <- postrank_mdomain_assess(history_input, dual, policy,   method = "mcmc", batch_size = 10L,   design = list(role = "synthetic_method_demonstration")) chain_table <- assessment[["native"]][["chain_table"]] knitr::kable(chain_table[chain_table[["event_id"]] == "joint-union",   c("chain_id", "n_retained", "hit_count", "rate", "max_zero_run",     "partial_batch_count")], digits = 3) assessment[["assurance"]][c("certificate_basis", "numerical_guarantee",   "convergence_established", "independence_established")] #> $certificate_basis #> [1] "empirical_diagnostic" #>  #> $numerical_guarantee #> [1] FALSE #>  #> $convergence_established #> [1] FALSE #>  #> $independence_established #> [1] FALSE

what: Building a multidomain input from joint states
title: Grading entities across multiple domains
text: Joint state arrays dimensions state x unit x domain, state slice holds units domains together cross-unit cross-domain dependence preserved. , two slices specify complete discrete posterior—putting probability 9/10 "usual" 1/10 "reversal" rather approximating continuous distribution two Monte Carlo draws: Every domain must already oriented larger values mean higher priority (orientation = "larger_is_higher"). domain’s target record, equality_classes declares structural model identities across units: giving unit class label states model force two units share identical target (even two units happen tie individual state): Next describe distribution came (provenance) combine states, target definitions, exact rational state probabilities (masses) postrank_mdomain_input(): postrank_mdomain_input() checks array dimensions, ID ordering, probability masses, required metadata fields; verify upstream model well specified properly sampled. Keep unit order domain order across targets, policy vectors, grade matrices (never pair separate domain simulations row number came joint state).
code: unit_ids <- c("Alder", "Birch", "Cedar") domain_ids <- c("attainment", "community") states <- array(NA_real_, c(2L, 3L, 2L),   dimnames = list(c("usual", "reversal"), unit_ids, domain_ids)) states["usual", , "attainment"] <- c(3, 2, 1) states["usual", , "community"] <- c(2, 3, 1) states["reversal", , "attainment"] <- c(2, 3, 1) states["reversal", , "community"] <- c(3, 2, 1) targets <- setNames(lapply(domain_ids, function(d) list(   definition = paste("Fictional", d, "priority coordinate"),   units = "illustrative score", orientation = "larger_is_higher",   transformations = list(),   equality_classes = setNames(unit_ids, unit_ids),   equality_provenance = "The model imposes no identity between distinct units." )), domain_ids) provenance <- list(   input_id = "three-unit-support", law_id = "fictional-two-state-law",   proper_law = TRUE, producer = "Self-contained teaching example",   conditioning_info = "No observations: this is a specified probability law.",   joint_generation = paste("Each labeled slice is one complete state",     "of all units and domains."),   sampling_assumptions = list(finite_support_origin = paste(     "These two states exhaust the specified fictional law;",     "they are not sampled draws.")) ) input <- postrank_mdomain_input(states, targets = targets,   provenance = provenance, representation = "exact_finite_law",   masses = c("9/10", "1/10")) input #> Multidomain posterior input #>  3 units; 2 domains; joint_array #>   Representation: exact_finite_law #>   Coupling: supplied_joint #>   Proper law: producer declaration; numerical guarantee: none

what: Choosing a decision rule and evaluating a profile card
title: Grading entities across multiple domains
text: policy gives equal weight ("1/2" "1/2") two domains, charges tau = "1/5" per unordered pair, omits per-domain expected-error budgets (q = NULL), bounds joint exceedance probability across domains alpha = "1/5" error-proportion threshold t = "0" (t = "0", single wrong-direction ordered pair either domain triggers exceedance event): Notice Alder profile (1, 2) Birch (2, 1): Alder ranks higher attainment Birch ranks higher community, single combined ranking forced onto two units. supplied finite distribution, card exact additive loss 1/30 (risk_exact) exact joint exceedance probability 1/10 (J_exact), satisfying alpha = "1/5" "reversal" state causes wrong-direction orders domains simultaneously counted union event: three units, every domain M = choose(3, 2) = 3 unordered pairs. Domain loss divides expected wrong-direction pairs plus tau times unordered pairs M, whereas protected error proportion divides wrong-direction pairs F N, number ordered (disclosed) pairs scope—triggering F / N > t (, F >= floor(t * N) + 1). Ordering two units strictly targets equal counts wrong-direction error. Within domain, units sharing domain’s equality_classes label must receive grade, even domain weight zero. Two units can therefore share attainment grade receive different community grades community model assigns distinct classes. column leaves pairs unordered (N = 0), error proportion eFDP NA, zero--withheld convention eFDP_zero 0 (eFDP_zero_exact equal "0"), F / N > t occur state (structural, distinct observing zero exceedances small Monte Carlo sample): Pass exact fractions decimal strings ("1/10" "0.1") postrank_mdomain_decision() whenever policy threshold exact rational number; bare R numeric literal 0.1 keeps binary floating-point value, can differ strict inequality boundaries. Integer grade labels encode order shared grades relabeled 1, 2, ... (10, 20, 30 defines exact card 1, 2, 3).
code: decision <- postrank_mdomain_decision(   weights = c(attainment = "1/2", community = "1/2"),   tau = "1/5", q = NULL, t = "0", alpha = "1/5")  G <- cbind(attainment = c(1, 2, 3), community = c(2, 1, 3)) rownames(G) <- unit_ids card <- postrank_mdomain_evaluate(input, G, decision) card #> Fixed multidomain report evaluation #>   3 units; 2 domains; mode: joint #>   Risk: 1/30; joint probability: 1/10 #>   Joint guards: evaluated; feasible_for_represented_measure #>   Basis: declared_finite_law; exact_represented_measure_arithmetic #>   Intended posterior feasibility certificate: none postrank_mdomain_grades(card) #>       attainment community #> Alder          1         2 #> Birch          2         1 #> Cedar          3         3 card[["domain_table"]][, c("domain_id", "N", "EF_exact", "loss_exact")] #>    domain_id N EF_exact loss_exact #> 1 attainment 3     1/10       1/30 #> 2  community 3     1/10       1/30 card[["event_table"]][, c("domain_id", "N", "cutoff_exact", "p_exact")] #>    domain_id N cutoff_exact p_exact #> 1 attainment 3            1    1/10 #> 2  community 3            1    1/10 card[["feasible_for_represented_measure"]] #> [1] TRUE withheld <- postrank_mdomain_evaluate(input, G * 0 + 1, decision) withheld[["scope_table"]][, c("domain_id", "N", "eFDP", "eFDP_zero")] #>    domain_id N eFDP eFDP_zero #> 1 attainment 0   NA         0 #> 2  community 0   NA         0 withheld[["status"]][["joint"]] #> [1] "analytic_zero"

what: Searching a declared set of candidate columns
title: Grading entities across multiple domains
text: postrank_mdomain_family() lists grade columns allowed domain original unit order (always including 1-grade -withheld column). two allowed columns two domains, Cartesian product contains four candidate report cards, postrank_mdomain_solve() evaluates four: Among four candidates, crossing card (risk_exact = "1/30", J_exact = "1/10") achieves smallest loss meeting joint exceedance cap. Optimality holds within declared candidate set: postrank_mdomain_solve() makes claim grade partitions outside family. multiple candidates tie minimum exact loss, tied optimizers flagged (optimal = TRUE) first lexicographic order renumbered (1..K_d) grade columns marked selected = TRUE. max_actions cap stops error enumerating oversized Cartesian product rather truncating search. build larger ordered candidate sets per domain, pass unit-ID permutations order allowed cutpoints cuts postrank_mdomain_family(). Choosing order = "posterior_mean" computes domain’s ordering supplied states records data-dependent choice metadata (independent held-validation).
code: family <- postrank_mdomain_family(input, columns = list(   attainment = list(setNames(G[, "attainment"], unit_ids)),   community = list(setNames(G[, "community"], unit_ids))),   max_actions = 4L) fit <- postrank_mdomain_solve(input, family, decision, max_actions = 4L) fit #> Multidomain candidate-family fit #>   4 declared actions examined; 1 optimizer (unique) #>   Risk: 1/30; joint probability: 1/10 #>   Scope: complete declared candidate product; unrestricted optimality not established #>   Search: candidate_restricted_exact_optimum_for_represented_measure #>   Intended posterior feasibility certificate: none fit[["candidate_table"]][, c("risk_exact", "J_exact",   "feasible_for_represented_measure", "optimal", "selected")] #>   risk_exact J_exact feasible_for_represented_measure optimal selected #> 1        1/5       0                             TRUE   FALSE    FALSE #> 2       7/60    1/10                             TRUE   FALSE    FALSE #> 3       7/60    1/10                             TRUE   FALSE    FALSE #> 4       1/30    1/10                             TRUE    TRUE     TRUE postrank_mdomain_grades(fit) #>       attainment community #> Alder          1         2 #> Birch          2         1 #> Cedar          3         3

what: Plotting three views of a multidomain card
title: Grading entities across multiple domains
text: postrank_plot_mdomain() renders three views stored card solved fit without running new evaluations. Setting domain_labels unit_labels relabels axes display keeping underlying IDs intact: Multidomain grade profiles Alder, Birch, Cedar across Attainment Community; Alder Grade 1 Attainment Grade 2 Community, whereas Birch reverses two grades. view = "cells" counts many units fall (attainment, community) grade combination keeping empty cells visible (profile cells two-dimensional grid rather single combined ranking): Occupied empty profile cells across three Attainment grades three Community grades, one unit (1, 2), (2, 1), (3, 3). view = "pair" compares two selected units across every domain (units filters drawn, caption losses exceedance probabilities still describe full report card): Pairwise domain comparison Alder Birch: Alder higher reported priority attainment Birch higher reported priority community.

what: Using posterior draws and choosing "exact", "iid", or "mcmc" assessment
title: Grading entities across multiple domains
text: posterior comes Monte Carlo simulation rather closed finite distribution, keep units domains draw together one slice unique draw IDs (can also pass existing validated postrank_draws object directly postrank_mdomain_input() provenance = list(input_id = ..., law_id = ..., proper_law = TRUE), leaving targets = NULL stored target definitions sampling metadata carry ). draw 20 independent states two-state distribution: Exact rational arithmetic (gmp) empirical draw counts finite distribution numerical guarantee intended posterior (intended_posterior_feasibility_certified FALSE). Match postrank_mdomain_assess() states produced: method = "iid": evaluates fixed-sample binomial tail check grade matrix, decision policy, target law, sample size, failure budget fixed drawing independent validation states (reusing states selected ordered card satisfy design). method = "mcmc": requires representation = "mcmc_equal_weight_draws" state_origin (source_index, chain_id, iteration_id supplied state order) computes descriptive chain batch summaries; zero observed exceedances chain summaries provide IID guarantee prove convergence. method = "exact": evaluates exact joint-exceedance probability complete exact_finite_law (describing finite distribution without checking model calibration, expected-error budgets q, optimality): See Separate domain rules versus joint multidomain protection cross-domain dependence examples MCMC chain diagnostics.
code: set.seed(120) draw_rows <- sample.int(2L, 20L, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.9, 0.1)) joint_draws <- states[draw_rows, , , drop = FALSE] dimnames(joint_draws)[[1L]] <- paste0("draw-", seq_len(20L)) draw_provenance <- provenance draw_provenance[["input_id"]] <- "three-unit-iid-draws" draw_provenance[["joint_generation"]] <- "Independent draws of complete two-domain states." draw_provenance[["sampling_assumptions"]] <- list(   iid_mechanism = "Independent categorical draws from the two-state law.",   target_assertion = "Each complete draw targets fictional-two-state-law." ) draw_input <- postrank_mdomain_input(joint_draws, targets = targets,   provenance = draw_provenance, representation = "iid_equal_weight_draws") draw_card <- postrank_mdomain_evaluate(draw_input, G, decision) draw_card[["assurance"]][c("numerical_basis",   "intended_posterior_feasibility_certified")] #> $numerical_basis #> [1] "supplied_empirical_measure" #>  #> $intended_posterior_feasibility_certified #> [1] FALSE assessed <- postrank_mdomain_assess(input, fit, method = "exact") assessed #> Fixed multidomain report assessment #>   Method: exact; status: evaluated_declared_finite_law #>   Risk: 1/30; joint probability: 1/10 #>   Joint certificate: yes; scope: specified declared-finite-law joint event only #>   Sampling assumptions verified: no; model calibration certified: no assessed[["certificate_scope"]] #> [1] "specified declared-finite-law joint event only"

title: Grading entities across multiple domains
text: Multidomain validation errors inherit class "postrank_mdomain_error" store machine-readable code field entries scripts can inspect failed without parsing error text. First, omitting joint_generation 3D state array stops provenance.joint_generation: Supply actual joint_generation statement states come one joint distribution, pass domain-named list 2D state x unit matrices within_domain_joint provenance domains come separate fits (never claim joint generation just separate fits number rows). Second, passing grade matrix whose row order differs input$unit_ids stops grades: Reorder rows columns name ([input$unit_ids, input$domain_ids, drop = FALSE]) rather overwriting rownames() colnames(), attach grades wrong units.
code: incomplete <- provenance incomplete[["joint_generation"]] <- NULL missing_joint <- tryCatch(   postrank_mdomain_input(states, targets = targets, provenance = incomplete,     representation = "exact_finite_law", masses = c("9/10", "1/10")),   postrank_mdomain_error = identity) c(code = missing_joint[["code"]], field = missing_joint[["field"]]) #>                          code                         field  #>       "mdomain_input_invalid" "provenance.joint_generation" reordered <- G[c("Birch", "Alder", "Cedar"), , drop = FALSE] bad_ids <- tryCatch(postrank_mdomain_evaluate(input, reordered, decision),   postrank_mdomain_error = identity) c(code = bad_ids[["code"]], field = bad_ids[["field"]]) #>                      code                     field  #> "mdomain_action_identity"                  "grades"  repaired <- reordered[input[["unit_ids"]], input[["domain_ids"]], drop = FALSE] postrank_mdomain_grades(postrank_mdomain_evaluate(input, repaired, decision)) #>       attainment community #> Alder          1         2 #> Birch          2         1 #> Cedar          3         3

title: Posterior Ranking with Integer Grades
text: Author maintainer: JoonHo Lee (jlee296@ua.edu). postrank assigns integer grades (1, 2, ..., G) entities—schools, employers, geographic areas—posterior draws, normal mixture distributions, precomputed pairwise comparison probabilities one several criteria. Grade 1 denotes highest priority. Assigning two entities different grades reports ordering ; assigning grade leaves pair unordered rather claiming underlying values equal. Grades minimize posterior expected wrong-direction errors (cost 1) plus cost tau pair left unordered grade, averaged entity pairs. Across multiple criteria, user-chosen weights combine criterion-specific losses one common grading, multidomain functions (postrank_mdomain_*) report separate grade per domain joint error-exceedance caps. Statistical model fitting takes place outside postrank; results conditional posterior supply.

Optimality postrank_mdomain_solve() holds within declared candidate set, exact arithmetic finite distribution sample verify model specification.
code: if (requireNamespace("gmp", quietly = TRUE)) {   ids <- c("Alder", "Birch")   domains <- c("attainment", "community")   x <- array(c(3, 2, 2, 3, 2, 3, 3, 2), c(2L, 2L, 2L),     dimnames = list(c("usual", "reversal"), ids, domains))   targets <- setNames(lapply(domains, function(d) list(     definition = paste("Fictional", d, "priority coordinate"),     units = "illustrative score", orientation = "larger_is_higher",     equality_classes = setNames(ids, ids),     equality_provenance = "No structural identity between distinct units."   )), domains)   provenance <- list(input_id = "readme-support", law_id = "readme-law",     proper_law = TRUE, producer = "Self-contained teaching example",     joint_generation = "Each slice is one complete state of both domains.",     sampling_assumptions = list(finite_support_origin =       "These two states exhaust the specified fictional law."))   input <- postrank_mdomain_input(x, targets = targets, provenance = provenance,     representation = "exact_finite_law", masses = c("9/10", "1/10"))   decision <- postrank_mdomain_decision(tau = "1/5", t = "0", alpha = "1/5")   G <- matrix(c(1, 2, 2, 1), 2L, dimnames = list(ids, domains))   card <- postrank_mdomain_evaluate(input, G, decision)   print(postrank_mdomain_grades(card))   print(postrank_plot_mdomain(card, view = "pair", units = ids)) } else {   message("Multidomain example skipped: install the optional package 'gmp'.") } #>       attainment community #> Alder          1         2 #> Birch          2         1

title: Prepare a Fully Described Posterior Input — as_postrank_draws
text: Three posterior forms accepted: joint_draws: equal-weight IID MCMC draws S x n x K array (keeping S x n x 1 K = 1), MCMC chain IDs, iteration numbers warmup/thinning history; criterion_blocks: separate equal-weight S_k x n matrices per criterion, preserving joint entity states within criterion without specifying dependence across criteria; finite_law: exact discrete posterior listing every positive-mass state safe-integer target values positive integer probability numerators summing common denominator (Monte Carlo sample; evaluating postrank_pairwise() requires optional gmp package). Values must already oriented larger values mean higher priority. Distinct entities must zero probability exact equality within criterion, observed ties stop call; posteriors positive probability ties, use as_postrank_tie_draws(). Required descriptions checked structure non-empty text without placeholder-word list postrank_declarations().

code: # Map the bundled two-criterion IID sample through posterior::draws_array: meta <- unclass(postrank_toy) meta$schema_version <- meta$input_schema_version meta$input_schema_version <- meta$validation <- NULL a <- meta$joint_draws$tensor$values map <- meta$joint_draws$variable_map var_ids <- vapply(map, `[[`, character(1), "source_target_variable_id") src_arr <- array(as.numeric(a), c(dim(a)[1], 1, length(map)),   dimnames = list(iteration = as.character(seq_len(dim(a)[1])),     chain = "1", variable = var_ids)) src <- posterior::as_draws_array(src_arr) coords <- lapply(seq_len(dim(a)[1]), function(s)   list(slot_id = dimnames(a)$draw[s], iteration_index = s, chain_index = 1L)) imported <- as_postrank_posterior(src, map, meta, coords) imported$validation$source_values_checked #> [1] TRUE identical(imported$joint_draws$tensor$values, a) #> [1] TRUE

Required top-level fields schema_version = "tie-aware-input-0.1", input_kind, dependence_mode = "joint_model", requested_functional = "expected_rank_loss", entity_ids, criterion_ids, targets, context, identification (status = "identified_declared"), tie_policy (rule = "equality_neutral", declared = TRUE, non-empty justification, observed_tie_action = "accept_declared_exact_equality"), provenance, equality, one joint_draws finite_law. Criterion-wise draw blocks, unequal draw weights, variational approximations rejected. equality list carries basis, non-empty justification, criterion_classes (criterion-named list character vectors assigning non-blank class label every entity): input_kind = "equal_weight_draws", joint_draws holds S x n x K array (retaining third dimension K = 1), equality$basis must "structural_declared". Entities sharing class label criterion k must identical values every retained draw (==, tolerance jitter). Coincident ties finitely many Monte Carlo draws never used merge structural classes, every retained numerical tie contributes empirical equality probability. pass rounded continuous draws ; re-export full precision postrank_draws(). input_kind = "exact_finite_posterior", finite_law lists positive-mass states safe-integer theta (n x K) positive safe-integer mass_numerator values summing denominator (2^53 - 1, verified optional package gmp), plus not_empirical_posterior_relabeling = TRUE. equality$basis must "exact_finite_law"; set criterion_classes = NULL derive partition equality across states (supplied partition must define equivalence relation). Integer values stored double JSON round-trips preserve exact storage. Structural checks verify model specification, MCMC convergence, scientific equality claims, issue numerical certificate. Mutating postrank_tie_draws object creation causes revalidation stop error.

title: Optimal or Quantile Cuts of a Declared Score Order — postrank_cuts
text: rule = "optimal" uses dynamic programming (ordinary floating-point arithmetic) minimize weighted expected loss contiguous partitions given score order G_max exact_G (breaking exact objective ties toward fewer occupied grades earlier block cuts). Optimality holds within contiguous partitions score order, across allowed gradings. rule = "quantile" assigns raw positional grades \(1 + \lfloor (p - 1) G_b / n \rfloor\) without optimization, merging grades straddled equal scores (can leave fewer G_b occupied grades, recorded warnings). Settings q error budgets objective = "minimax" stop unsupported_baseline_settings, exact_G exceeding number distinct score blocks stops exact_G_exceeds_blocks (baseline_exact_grade_violation quantile merging leaves fewer grades). postrank_probabilities() inputs support --G_max cuts without exact_G, whereas postrank_pairwise postrank_coefficients also allow exact_G.

title: Assess a Fixed Multidomain Grade Profile — postrank_mdomain_assess
text: three methods differ compute assume: Conditional fixed-sample IID (method = "iid"): generating inspecting validation draws, fix candidate report card separate exploration draws save card$receipts$validation_spec_hashes (report, decision, target_law, exclude draw rows). Supply design : spec_hashes equal three-element list; beta_exact equal reduced fraction string beta ("1/20"); six TRUE flags (iid_whole_states, independent_of_exploration, frozen_before_validation, fixed_sample_size, no_validation_reuse, no_optional_stopping); five non-blank strings (iid_mechanism, independence_justification, exploration_history_id, frozen_record_id, validation_batch_id); fixed_S matching validation draw count S; validation_state_ids matching validation state IDs order; exploration_state_ids (unique character vector, possibly character(), disjoint validation_state_ids).   Descriptive MCMC (method = "mcmc"): Computes empirical hit counts, zero-hit runs, fixed-size batch summaries (retaining final partial batch) supplied chain order. joint_certificate always FALSE (diagnostics_not_certificate = TRUE): batch summaries imply independent replicates, IID/binomial inference, MCMC convergence, held-validation, zero observed hits establish J = 0 unless event analytically impossible (N = 0). Declared finite law (method = "exact"): Evaluates grades across states "exact_finite_law" input (status = "evaluated_declared_finite_law"). Floating-point state masses summed floating-point arithmetic rather converted exact rationals (reported evaluation$status$arithmetic). joint_certificate records whether J <= alpha declared finite law, numerical guarantee underlying continuous posterior discretized states floating-point masses used.
code: Given `v` observed joint-event violations out of `S` coupled validation draws, the method tests \eqn{H_0: J > \alpha} against \eqn{H_1: J \le \alpha} at Monte Carlo Type-I error level `beta`, setting `joint_certificate = TRUE` and `status = "certified_conditional_on_declared_iid_independence"` when the exact `gmp` rational binomial lower tail \eqn{\Pr(\mathrm{Binomial}(S, \alpha) \le v)} is at most `beta` (`upper_display` is an approximate \eqn{1 - \beta} one-sided upper bound on `J` for display only). Hash and disjoint-ID checks verify internal consistency only and cannot prove prior fixation or independence; non-acceptance returns `"inconclusive"`, which does not prove `J > alpha`. Analytically zero union events (`"analytic_zero_event"`) and `alpha = 1` (`"trivial_alpha_one"`) set `joint_certificate = TRUE` without requiring `design`, while disabled joint protection sets `status = "joint_protection_disabled"` and `joint_certificate = FALSE`.

text: components Non-empty plain named list state records (names(components) unique state IDs). Every state must share exact entity_ids (n >= 2) criterion_ids (K >= 1) identical order, element may carry extra R attributes: mu: finite numeric vector named criterion_ids recording shared state h's criterion-level hyperparameter mean (checked stored provenance/identity); Sigma: finite symmetric positive-definite K x K matrix (Sigma == t(Sigma) zero tolerance) dimnames = list(criterion_i = criterion_ids, criterion_j = criterion_ids), recording shared state h's criterion-level hyperparameter covariance; means: finite n x K precomputed entity conditional posterior mean matrix given h, dimnames = list(entity = entity_ids, criterion = criterion_ids) (larger values mean higher priority; used directly compute mixture means e); covariance: finite symmetric positive-definite K x K x n array within-entity conditional posterior covariances given h (every slice must satisfy S == t(S) zero tolerance; symmetrize (V + t(V)) / 2 beforehand needed), dimnames named criterion_i, criterion_j, entity (criterion_ids, criterion_ids, entity_ids). covariance links criteria within entity ; cross-entity dependence enters shared state h. weights Nonnegative finite plain numeric state probabilities named names(components) component order, summing one within 1e-12 (never rescaled automatically, extra R attributes). source_regime = "hyperparameter_mcmc", weights must equal 1 / length(components). mixture probabilities states, criterion loss weights. state_index Base data.frame (tibble extra attributes) component order, state_id matching names(components). source_regime = "fixed_finite_mixture", state_id column; source_regime = "hyperparameter_mcmc", columns must c("state_id", "chain_id", "iteration") positive integer chain original iteration numbers unique (chain_id, iteration) pairs. source_regime "fixed_finite_mixture" specified finite mixture quadrature rule, "hyperparameter_mcmc" retained hyperparameter MCMC states. conditional_independence Must "entities_given_shared_h", explicit model declaration (inferred marginal moments) stating entities conditionally independent given shared state h. provenance Plain named list non-empty character strings (extra R attributes): producer_id, producer_version, posterior_id, input_payload_sha256, source_sha256, config_sha256, plus optional model_sha256. code: state <- function(d) {   ks <- "score"; ids <- c("A", "B")   list(mu = c(score = d),     Sigma = matrix(1, 1, 1,       dimnames = list(criterion_i = ks, criterion_j = ks)),     means = matrix(c(d, 0.4), 2, 1,       dimnames = list(entity = ids, criterion = ks)),     covariance = array(0.5, c(1, 1, 2),       dimnames = list(criterion_i = ks, criterion_j = ks, entity = ids))) } comps <- list(low = state(-1), high = state(0.5)) cfg <- list(weights = c(low = 0.5, high = 0.5),   state_index = data.frame(state_id = c("low", "high")),   source_regime = "fixed_finite_mixture",   conditional_independence = "entities_given_shared_h") prov <- list(producer_id = "postrank_mixture_coefficients help example",   producer_version = "1", posterior_id = "two-state-normal-mixture",   input_payload_sha256 = digest::digest(comps, algo = "sha256"),   source_sha256 = digest::digest(body(state), algo = "sha256"),   config_sha256 = digest::digest(cfg, algo = "sha256")) x <- postrank_mixture_coefficients(comps, cfg$weights, cfg$state_index,   cfg$source_regime, cfg$conditional_independence, prov) x$e[, , "score"] #>         entity_j #> entity_i         A         B #>        A        NA 0.6897078 #>        B 0.3102922        NA validate_postrank_coefficients(x, recompute = TRUE)
